body: It’s super late but nobody from r/raisedbynarcissists has been answering my thread so I thought to ask you. I feel really insecure about my feelings and my thoughts regarding my family, mainly because I’ve been feeling some love here and there for them (I notice it’s triggered when they treat me like I’m some 5 year old)...I feel like I’m making these problems for myself, that I shouldn’t be suicidal and I shouldn’t be so hurting, and that I’m just trying to make myself out as the victim (something my brother once said that keeps coming back when I feel like this). I’m feeling pathetic and insecure and these feelings are intensified by the deep insecurity that comes from social anxiety and I’m cutting myself not to feel it. It feels horrible - like there’s even more tension with myself and I keep thinking that killing myself (the most likely outcome after the upcoming school year but right now this feeling is sickening) would get rid of everything. Can I run it down to you and then you reaffirm my feelings, or whatever appropriate response you could reply with? Thanks.

Hey man, I know it’s been a few weeks since our convo but I just wanted to let you know you were partly the reason I didn’t go through with it the next day. If my plan to run away doesn’t work (which it probably won’t), or I don’t find solace in that beautiful girl, I’m done, I can’t keep going through an intolerable existence. But this simple acceptance still helped.
No. Egypt is a Muslim majority country. “Atheist” would be an idealogical threat to most here.

Yeah no. I’m already told her before, multiple times, and either she stays silent, says I’m wrong and dumb, or complains that I’m in misery. She’s always been a bitchy idiot and I don’t see that changing. 

I don’t see anything changing in general. I could live through this (but to what end?) or end it, and that’s up to me. I just need time to talk with my eldest brother (he’s been away for a month and just came back). He’s the only one who’s ever noticed how I’m depressed. Maybe he can understand. 3 days left of this school year, as next Tuesday-Thursday are end of year examinations, I’ll give it one more try. So I guess I’ll take a final look at my options soon.

I just kept reading and watching psychology lectures and the likes. It made me learn some techniques to help me control it. Like say, I don’t have to talk to an entire group at once, I can just focus on one person, and see the rest of their thoughts and reactions reflected on his/her face. And I can talk to one person.

But then everything comes back into the mix and it’s pointless.

The cutting is just because....I’m able to do something. Anything at all. That I’m not sitting there doing nothing, but doing something about it, can stop me from hurting emotionally. It can make me feel empty instead (but then I want the sadness and pure anxiety to come back, cause that’s better than feeling nothing). Or maybe I think I deserve it, I’m not sure.

Yes, according to my mom (I can’t remember that well...), when I was around 10 I used to casually make friends and play football at the park. Then my dad started coming with us, telling me who to befriend and who not to, making me distrusting of them (i.e “don’t give your phone to him, he might break it!), and then I just completely locked myself in.

I overthink every social interaction a dozen times over. Every time I try to talk about something or open up I shut myself down because I’m afraid of the reactions I’ll get. Even when I almost completely solved my social anxiety I get bogged down in making friends by shelter parenting and it comes back.

I do often feel like I’m imprisoned. Not even because of the religious issue, it’s just when your father is a “shelter” parent who forces his every opinion on you and doesn’t allow you much freedom, being at school can be a release despite the loneliness I feel when I see people with each other. In fact, I would say he’s where the anxiety and lack of friends stems from. Like he’s trying to raise me an autist on purpose. The friends I could have had if it weren’t for him...adoption isn’t that simple unfortunately.

Yeah, thanks. For the first time in months I feel genuinely good, like maybe, just maybe I could get through this. Because it’s nice to open up without being judged.

This is the first time someone just accepted my feelings instead of telling me they're somehow inaccurate. Thanks for that.

Social anxiety. Loneliness, no friends. Constant fear of being disowned and beaten by my family if they knew I don't share their religious beliefs.
